summary.headline: Paras Healthcare Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to Rs 511 crore, with H1 PAT of Rs 90 crore against Rs 44 crore for full FY26.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was Rs 511 crore, up 23% YoY and 8.6% QoQ, with H1 revenue of Rs 981 crore (up 25%). Operating EBITDA (excluding other income) rose 47% YoY to Rs 120 crore in Q2, with margin gains attributed mainly to material cost efficiency, formulary compliance and case mix. Group occupancy rose to 76.3% in Q2 from 62.5%, and new hospitals (Srinagar and Ludhiana) moved to positive EBITDA. Working capital absorbed Rs 172 crore in H1, with receivables rising from Rs 350 crore in March to Rs 518 crore, and net debt stands at Rs 620 crore after IPO-funded repayments.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Darbhanga)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8.5% in Q2 and 9.1% in H1; Q2 operating EBITDA margin 29.6% (up 360 bps YoY), H1 margin 28.9%; H1 occupancy 76.5%.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (Ranchi, Jaipur-area unit as named 'Adepur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27.2% in Q2 and 43.2% in H1; H1 EBITDA margin 18.3% vs 12.4%; H1 occupancy 68.6% vs 49.1%. Ranchi reported 25.8% margin in Q2.

segments.name: New hospitals (Srinagar, Ludhiana as named 'Vlampur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 139% in Q2 and 147% in H1; operating EBITDA turned positive at Rs 15.8 crore in Q2 (vs negative Rs 13 crore in FY26); H1 margin 18.7%; H1 occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance given; management said trends can be used for modelling.
Long-term steady-state blended operating margin targeted in the mid-20s range; management said this is a playbook, not guidance.
About 200-250 beds yet to open (Kanpur wings and Ranchi), taking operational beds from ~1,500 toward ~1,800; Kanpur and Ranchi additions expected by end of FY27.
Gurgaon adds ~300 beds (golf course extension) and Ludhiana ~500 beds over the next 12-18 months, per management.
Operating EBITDA margin (excl. other income) expected to stay in the 2.8-3x range... (AOL figure) management expects this trend to continue.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 90 crore in H1 across various units, plus payments for a new Gurugram-area unit (transcript: 'Gulbagh 2').
Dandhi (Darbhanga) has 435 beds; roughly half opened, with two more wings pending.
Kanpur: more beds to be opened by end of FY27; impanelments under insurance and government schemes completed.
Robotic surgery programs running at Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula and newly launched at Ranchi; liver transplant extended from Gurgaon to Panchkula and Patna.
Management said expansion would be asset-light; acquisitions are low priority given current commitments, though not ruled out.
demand_pricing: Group occupancy 76.3% in Q2 FY27 vs 62.5% YoY; H1 occupancy 73% vs 59%.
Kanpur occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27.
Revenue mix H1 FY27: cash/self-pay 32%, insurance 24%, government schemes and PSUs ~44% (as stated in transcript, partly garbled).
Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals including Udaipur; company says it has recovered 30-40% of state scheme business there.
Management says payor-mix shift toward cash and insurance is a stated priority, with marketing and tertiary/quaternary programs to drive it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Udaipur soft in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rajasthan state government scheme was reviewed and temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals in the state; Udaipur overall business grew in absolute terms and about 30-40% of state scheme business has been recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How has Kanpur ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27, driven by new empanelments, more clinicians and a specialty-focused mix; Kanpur insurance and government scheme empanelments are complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital absorb so much cash despite profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Rs 172 crore outflow to DSO rising from ~79 to ~92 days, from the 25% business growth, faster growth at new hospitals, payor mix and lumpy payments from certain peer groups; it expects normalisation as mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 50 crore item in other financial assets?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a long-term fixed deposit made from the Rs 80 crore equity infusion in April 2025, reclassified as other financial assets because it is non-current.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin for mature hospitals and how new hospitals should evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a lifecycle: new hospitals start negative, reach mid-to-high teens, then emerging, then mature at mid-to-high 20s; the blended steady state should be in the mid-20s, though no formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the low AOL-type operating loss per bed continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operating loss figure has consistently been in the 2.8-3 range and expects it to continue, helped by case mix (oncology, radiation, robotics, transplants) and occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Is there headroom to grow occupancy in mature hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Patna and Panchkula have further room; Gurgaon is constrained, which is why the golf course extension is planned. Darbhanga remains a feeder to Patna while adding tertiary programs.

qa_highlights.question: How long will emerging hospitals take to reach mature margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said emerging hospitals typically take 4 to 7 years to move to the mature bucket; Ranchi already delivers mid-20s margins and may be reclassified.

risks_watch: Receivables build-up (Rs 518 crore, DSO ~92 days) and its normalisation in H2.
Rajasthan government scheme suspension and its effect on Udaipur and other state-scheme-dependent revenue.
Execution of 200-250 bed openings in Kanpur and Ranchi and the Gurgaon and Ludhiana expansions over the next 12-18 months.
Payor mix: government and PSU share of revenue, and the pace of shift to cash and insurance.
Gross debt of Rs 979 crore and net debt of Rs 620 crore; pro forma debt Rs 143 crore post IPO repayments.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and margin trajectory, with clear quantified KPIs; cautious and non-committal on forward guidance, repeatedly declining to give numbers. Working capital and state-scheme questions were answered with explanation rather than commitment.
key_quotes: Most of the gains in margin improvement were a result of improvement in material cost, again a result of procurement efficiency, formulary compliances and case mix.
I'm not giving a guidance on that but that is the model playbook which we are looking at.
So the blended every time which we are looking at in the long steady state should be in the mid 20s range.

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management says trends can be used for modelling, with 200-250 beds (Kanpur, Ranchi) due by end FY27 plus ~300 Gurgaon and ~500 Ludhiana beds in 12-18 months, while occupancy rose to 76.3% from 62.5% and Q2 revenue grew 23% YoY.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 operating EBITDA margin rose to about 23% (Rs 120 cr on Rs 511 cr revenue) vs ~14% a year ago, mature hospitals at 29.6%, and management expects the operating-loss-per-bed trend to continue with the mid-20s blended steady state as a playbook, not guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 200-250 beds (Kanpur wings, Ranchi) are under construction with Kanpur and Ranchi additions due by end FY27, plus Gurgaon (~300 beds) and Ludhiana (~500 beds) over the next 12-18 months, taking operational beds from ~1,500 toward ~1,800.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Group occupancy rose to 76.3% in Q2 from 62.5% and H1 revenue grew 25%, with Kanpur occupancy at 78.4% and new capacity coming online, though Rajasthan scheme suspension is a drag.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs 90 cr capex in H1 and a new Gurugram-area unit (Gulbagh 2) are already in progress, but management said expansion is asset-light and acquisitions are low priority, so no fresh capex programme was announced; utilisation at 76.3% is near the threshold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal revenue or margin guidance was given, and management declined to give numbers, though occupancy and margin trends are running ahead of the implied trajectory.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables rose to Rs 518 cr (DSO ~92 days from ~79) and working capital absorbed Rs 172 cr in H1, plus the Rajasthan state scheme suspension affects Udaipur, with about 30-40% of that business recovered so far.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Robotic surgery launched at Ranchi and liver transplant extended to Panchkula and Patna; tertiary and quaternary programmes are being pushed to drive payor-mix shift, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: DSO normalisation from ~92 days
rows.why: Working capital absorbed Rs 172 cr in H1 as DSO rose from ~79 to ~92 days, and management expects normalisation as payor mix improves, though it has not given a number or date.

rows.label: Net debt reduction after IPO repayments
rows.why: Rs 375 cr term debt repaid, bringing pro forma debt to Rs 143 cr against gross borrowings of Rs 979 cr in September and cash of Rs 360 cr, with net debt at Rs 620 cr.

rows.label: Emerging hospitals moving to mature bucket
rows.why: Ranchi already delivers a 25.8% Q2 margin and may be reclassified as mature, though management says emerging hospitals typically take 4-7 years to mature.

tone.note: Management was confident on occupancy, Kanpur ramp-up and margin trajectory, but cautious on formal guidance and declined to give numbers; analysts probed working capital build-up, the Rajasthan state scheme suspension, and the sustainability of the operating-loss-per-bed metric.
